changes.new: Separately, \textcite{darcet2024vision} mitigated high-norm artifact tokens with registers. The ResLRP preprint targets attribution instability caused by cancellation between opposing residual branches. Its residual $\gamma$-rule conserves relevance and bounds absolute relevance amplification by a factor of $1+2/\gamma$ at each backward merge, assuming a nonzero residual output and $\gamma>0$ \parencite{Berend2026ResLRP}.
changes.evidence: Opposing residual branches can amplify backward relevance. For nonzero residual outputs and gamma>0 the residual gamma-rule conserves relevance and bounds absolute relevance amplification by 1+2/gamma per merge; the guarantee is local and structural, not forward-DC numerical stability or faithfulness.

changes.evidence: The modified x*detach(g(x)/x) activation realizes the LRP identity rule under Gradient-times-Input. GELU is explicitly included. This local identity does not imply global RG, generalized alpha-beta, or LayerNorm equivalence.
